findings.description: `host.endswith(domain)` has no label boundary. With partner domain `shop.example`, an attacker-registered `https://evilshop.example` or `https://notshop.example` passes. The response then echoes that origin with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, so the attacker's page can call /v1/balance and /v1/redeem with the member's session cookie and read the responses. Redeeming points on the member's behalf is possible too.
findings.suggestion: Match the exact domain or a true subdomain: `host == domain or host.endswith('.' + domain)`.
findings.title: Partner domain match uses endswith without a dot boundary, allowing look-alike origins with credentials

findings.description: `parts.hostname` drops the port and userinfo, so `https://user@shop.example:8443` is treated as the partner host. The original origin string is then echoed back in Access-Control-Allow-Origin. A browser never sends such an origin, but any non-browser caller can. The exact-origin path compares the full string, so the two paths are inconsistent.
findings.suggestion: Reject origins that have a port or userinfo (compare `parts.netloc` to `parts.hostname`) unless explicitly allowed.
findings.title: Port in origin not rejected for partner origins, and response echoes non-normalised origin
